purpose: Darolutamide is used to treat prostate cancer. It is specifically used for men who have non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, meaning the cancer has not spread to other parts of the body but is still growing despite having low testosterone levels. It may also be used for metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer in combination with other treatments.
how_it_works: Prostate cancer cells need the male hormone testosterone to grow. Darolutamide works by blocking the androgen receptor, which is like locking the door that testosterone uses to enter cancer cells. Without that signal, the cancer cells have a harder time growing and spreading.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include feeling tired or fatigued, pain in your arms or legs, a rash on your skin, and an increase in certain liver enzyme levels in your blood. Some people also experience falls, broken bones, or heart problems, so it is important to stay active and be careful to avoid falls.
warnings: Darolutamide can harm an unborn baby, so men taking this drug should use effective birth control with a female partner who could become pregnant during treatment and for at least one week after the last dose. Tell your doctor right away if you have any heart problems, liver disease, or seizure history. This medicine can also increase the risk of falls and fractures, so be cautious about your balance and bone health.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 600 mg (two 300 mg tablets) taken by mouth twice a day, with food. That means you take it in the morning and again in the evening with meals. Try to take it at the same times each day and swallow the tablets whole.
